schema_notes:
v5.17 fixes a joint_stress tagging gap: 65 exercises that require a sustained flexed-wrist grip to perform - hanging/pulling from a bar, rings, or hangboard (Pull-up Bar / Rings / Climbing Hangboard equipment), and heavy strongman-style grip carries/holds (Farmer Handles, Conan's Wheel, Fingal's Fingers) - had no 'Wrist' tag in joint_stress, so the injury-safety engine never screened them against wrist injuries (e.g. a person with a severity-3 'Wrist Flexor Tendons - Complete Rupture' entry was still being prescribed Chin-Up, Weighted Pull-Up, Farmer Handles Carry, etc., since the engine only excludes/derisks an exercise for a joint that's actually listed in its joint_stress). 'Wrist' was appended to the existing joint_stress list for each of the 65 affected exercises; no other field changed. See ROADMAP/PR notes for the full before/after exercise list.

v4.0 adds movement-analysis and athletic-quality-tag fields to every exercise, derived from each exercise's existing category/pattern/equipment/difficulty (see exercise_metadata.py). All v3.0 fields are unchanged.

v5.1 adds 26 new exercises focused on the categories/equipment that were thin in v5.0: Dumbbell (3 -> 17), Jump (2 -> 8), Power (1 -> 7), and Grip (2 -> 6), plus a few Conditioning entry points below the existing high-difficulty-only entries. All are enriched through the same exercise_metadata.enrich_exercise() pipeline as the rest of the database, so movement-analysis and athletic-quality fields follow the same rules. No existing exercise or field was changed.

v5.1.1 fixes a gap where JOINT_STABILITY_TAG (exercise_metadata.py, duplicated and out of sync in knowledge_graph.py) only covered 5 of the 8 joints joint_stress actually uses - Wrist, Elbow, and Lower Back had no stability tag at all, so knowledge_graph.py silently dropped stresses_joint edges for those joints and no exercise could ever be a rehab candidate for an injury on them. Added 'Wrist Stability', 'Elbow Stability', and 'Lower Back Stability' to ATHLETIC_QUALITY_TAGS and JOINT_STABILITY_TAG (now the single source of truth, imported by knowledge_graph.py instead of copy-pasted), then re-ran enrich_exercise() over every exercise to backfill the 3 new tags. No other field changed.

v5.2 adds 182 new exercises (generate_batch4_pl_oly_strongman.py) covering powerlifting bar/accommodating-resistance variations (box/pin/pause/tempo/banded/chain squats & benches, safety-bar/buffalo-bar/cambered-bar work), Olympic lifting pulls and receiving positions (hang/block/muscle/tall clean & snatch variants, high pulls), strongman implements (atlas stone, log, axle, sandbag, yoke-family carries), classic rows, and a handful of missing commercial machines (V-squat, pendulum squat, chest/shoulder press machines, lever row/press). Requested names already covered by an existing exercise (e.g. 'Anderson Squat', 'Push Press', 'Rack Pull', 'Split Jerk') were skipped rather than duplicated. All 182 were run through the same enrich_exercise() pipeline as the rest of the database.

v5.6 adds 5 new exercises (generate_batch5_manual_part7_gaps.py, 442 -> 447) closing the last gap in Combat Sports & Rugby S&C Manual Part 7/7.7 alignment: Band-Assisted Pull-Up, Band-Assisted Dip, Landmine Anti-Rotation Press (Half-Kneeling), Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Press, and Fat-Grip Row. Run through the same enrich_exercise() pipeline as the rest of the database; zero dangling progression/regression/alternative references and DAG acyclicity verified after the merge.

v5.7 adds 45 new exercises (generate_batch6_thin_equipment.py) to the 14 machine/cable/band/medicine-ball equipment types that were thinnest relative to how common they are in a real commercial gym (Cable Machine 3->11, Lat Pulldown 3->6, Leg Press 2->5, Leg Curl 2->4, Leg Extension 1->3, Seated Row 2->5, Chest Press Machine 1->3, Shoulder Press Machine 1->3, Pec Deck 1->3, Smith Machine 3->7, Hack Squat Machine 1->3, High Row Machine 1->3, Resistance Band 6->12, Medicine Ball 4->8). Enriched through the same exercise_metadata.enrich_exercise() pipeline as the rest of the database, but applied only to these 45 new ids (enrich_batch6_only.py) rather than re-running enrich_exercises.py over the whole file, since that script's version/schema_notes overwrite would have reverted this file's version history and its re-derivation is not perfectly idempotent on exercises that were already enriched. No pre-existing exercise or field was changed.

v5.8 adds 66 new exercises (generate_batch7_equipment_rehab.py). Two things: (1) equipment depth - the 15 equipment types sitting at exactly 1 exercise and 12 sitting at exactly 2 each get +2, so every equipment type in the database now has at least 3 (most at least 4) instead of unlocking 1-2 repeats when picked. (2) rehab gap - querying is_rehab_candidate() (knowledge_graph.py) against the pre-batch7 file showed Neck had ZERO rehab-candidate exercises at any severity (no exercise trained Neck stability at a low enough difficulty to qualify) and Ankle had only 6 next to Shoulder/Hip/Knee's 50+. Added 6 difficulty=2 Neck-stability exercises and 6 difficulty=2 Ankle-stability exercises - difficulty=2 is the ceiling is_rehab_candidate() enforces, and 30 + difficulty*8 = 46 clears the 40 stability-quality floor the joint_stress loop awards, so both joints have real rehab candidates for the first time / at real depth. Two new equipment types (Neck Harness, Balance Board) were added for the rehab work, plus a new 'Rehab & Mobility' group in exercise_metadata.py's EQUIPMENT_CATEGORIES so they're grouped correctly in the equipment catalog instead of falling into 'Other'. Enriched through the same exercise_metadata.enrich_exercise() pipeline as the rest of the database, applied only to these 66 new ids (enrich_batch7_only.py), same reasoning as enrich_batch6_only.py for why. No pre-existing exercise or field was changed.

v5.9 adds 100 new exercises (generate_batch8_equipment_depth.py). Closes out the equipment-depth pass batch6/7 started: the 50 equipment types still sitting at only 3 or 4 exercises (mostly single-purpose machines, specialty bars, strongman implements, and conditioning tools batch6's general-machine pass and batch7's 1-2-count/rehab pass didn't reach) each get +2, following the exact same per-equipment pattern as those two batches. No equipment type in the database is under 5 exercises anymore. Enriched through the same exercise_metadata.enrich_exercise() pipeline as the rest of the database, applied only to these 100 new ids (enrich_batch8_only.py), same reasoning as enrich_batch6/7_only.py for why. No pre-existing exercise or field was changed. Follow-up: Balance Board (v5.9) started at 2 exercises, so +2 only reached 4 — one more added here (balanceboard_pushup_001) so it reaches 5 like every other equipment type in the database.

v5.10 adds 72 new exercises (generate_batch9_equipment_depth2.py). Follow-up to batch8: the 36 equipment types batch8 left sitting exactly at the 5-exercise floor (isolation machines, strongman implements, and combat/conditioning tools) each get +2 more, same per-equipment pattern as batch6/7/8. Every equipment type touched by this batch is now at 7 exercises. Enriched through the same exercise_metadata.enrich_exercise() pipeline as the rest of the database, applied only to these 72 new ids (enrich_batch9_only.py), same reasoning as enrich_batch6/7/8_only.py for why. No pre-existing exercise or field was changed.

v5.11 fixes an injury-naming mismatch between data/exercises.json and backend/services/injury_taxonomy.py: 15 of the 31 distinct injuries_to_avoid strings in use across the file (243 exercises) did not exactly match any INJURY_TAXONOMY entry name, so progression_engine._resolve_injury_severity() silently could not find them and those exercises fell back to flat literal-tag matching instead of the severity-tiered four-tier risk model every other exercise gets. 7 of those strings were near-duplicates of an existing taxonomy entry under slightly different formatting (e.g. "Golfer's Elbow" vs. "Medial Epicondylalgia (Golfer's Elbow)", "Shoulder Instability" vs. "Shoulder Instability (General/Atraumatic)") and are renamed here to the exact canonical taxonomy name (243 exercises touched, injuries_to_avoid only - no other field on any exercise changed, verified by diffing every exercise by id before/after). The remaining 8 ("Low Back Pain", "Rotator Cuff", "Achilles", "Patellar Tendon", "Hamstring Strain", "Wrist Pain", "Neck Pain", "Lower Back Strain") are genuinely non-specific/ungraded terms with no single correct graded equivalent, so instead of forcing a guessed grade onto hundreds of exercises, injury_taxonomy.py gained a matching severity-1 umbrella entry for each (see injury_taxonomy.py's "Bare/vernacular umbrella terms" section) - zero exercises.json changes needed for those 8. injury_taxonomy.py separately gained 11 new named conditions covering head and thorax injuries relevant to the combat/collision sports this app targets and previously missing entirely: 3 graded Concussion entries, 2 Rib Fracture entries, 2 Intercostal Muscle Strain grades, Costochondritis, and Sports Hernia (Athletic Pubalgia). v5.18 adds a five-field grouping taxonomy to every exercise — is_compound (bool), is_olympic_lift (bool), push_pull ('Push'/'Pull'/null), upper_lower ('Upper'/'Lower'/'Full Body'/'Core'), and chain_emphasis ('Posterior'/'Anterior'/'Mixed') — so the library and session builder can filter/group by these axes directly. All derived from existing fields (name, category, movement_pattern, primary/secondary_muscles) via exercise_metadata.derive_taxonomy_groups(); no hand-typed values. is_compound corrects for category NOT tracking compound vs. isolation (e.g. curls and pushdowns share a category with genuinely multi-joint lifts) by checking movement-name keywords plus a single-primary-muscle/no-secondary/no-stabilizer fallback. is_olympic_lift flags Clean/Snatch/Jerk and their standard training variants, excluding the 5 exercises that only borrow the clean/snatch grip on an ordinary squat/deadlift/RDL. push_pull is null (not just Push/Pull) for patterns it doesn't apply to, e.g. Squat/Hinge/Carry. chain_emphasis weights primary muscles 2x vs. secondary 1x and requires a >=1.3x lean to call Posterior/Anterior, otherwise Mixed. No other field changed.

v5.19 adds exercise-specific connective-tissue & phase biomechanics to every exercise: tendons_loaded (which tendon transmits force at each joint in joint_stress, tagged prime_mover vs. stabilizer, push- vs. pull-tendon picked via the v5.18 push_pull field), ligaments_stressed (which ligament resists an unwanted motion at that joint - listed ONLY when this specific exercise's already-derived tissue-demand flags, from derive_tissue_demands(), imply that motion is actually present, e.g. ACL only appears for shear/impact/unilateral-loaded knee work, not every knee exercise), muscle_action_by_phase (prime movers/synergists/stabilizers split across Isometric Hold, or Eccentric Preload -> Concentric Drive for SSC movements, or Eccentric -> Concentric for standard biphasic lifts, keyed off force_type), and biomechanics_notes (a generated prose summary of the above, per exercise). All derived from fields already on the exercise (joint_stress, force_type, category, and the already-existing derive_tissue_demands() signals) via exercise_metadata.derive_connective_tissue() — no hand-typed per-exercise values; the underlying anatomy (which tendon/ligament crosses which joint) is standard gross anatomy, not invented. No other field changed.

v5.35 removes a true duplicate entry: "Prone Y-T-W Raise" existed twice, under prone_ytw_raise_001 (the fuller entry - populated sport_priority, movement_family, in_manual, push_pull, and a progressions link to doorframe_row_001) and back_prone_ytw_001 (a thinner duplicate with the same name/muscles/joint_stress/injuries_to_avoid but missing those fields, and referenced nowhere else in the file as a progression/regression/alternative). Also hardened the FORGE S&C Template Library <-> exercises.json name matcher (backend/services/sc_template_library.py), after auditing all ~19.8k template exercise-name references against exercises.json and finding ~8.1k (165 distinct names) falling through both the exact and fuzzy match to an unchecked "Unverified" passthrough (no equipment/injury gate applied). Three changes, all conservative and test-covered:
  - Added "med" -> "medicine" to _ABBREVIATIONS, so "Med-Ball Russian Twist" normalizes the same as exercises.json's own "Medicine Ball Russian Twist".
  - Split the equipment-word vocabulary into _SETUP_QUALIFIER_WORDS (rack/weighted/assisted/resistance - safe to add or drop on either side of a match) and _BASE_TOOL_WORDS (barbell/dumbbell/kettlebell/cable/machine/ez-bar/etc - naming a genuinely different tool), and require that a token-diff match name at most one _BASE_TOOL_WORDS concept. An earlier version of this pass allowed any equipment-vocabulary symmetric difference through, which turned out to silently bridge real equipment swaps ("DB Lateral Raise" -> "Cable Lateral Raise", "Barbell Curl" -> "EZ Bar Curl", "Preacher Curl Machine" -> "Dumbbell Preacher Curl") - exactly the kind of wrong match that corrupts the equipment/injury gate instead of feeding it. The at-most-one-base-tool guard closes that. "belt" and "vest" were deliberately left out of both word-sets entirely (see the comment beside _BASE_TOOL_WORDS) - a dip belt and a weighted vest are different props for adding load, and letting either be bridged as an implicit default invented equipment requirements a template never asked for (a plain "Box Jump" must not resolve to "Weighted Vest Box Jump").
  - Added a short hand-checked _NAME_ALIASES list (back squat -> Barbell Back Squat, bench press -> Flat Bench Press, reverse hyper -> Reverse Hyperextension, barbell/dumbbell curl -> their Standing ... db entries) for a handful of very common colloquial names the token-diff algorithm can't safely resolve on its own, because exercises.json's matching entry carries its own base-tool word too ("Barbell Back Squat") rather than leaving it implicit.
  Net effect: template exercise-name match rate rose from 33.6% to 60.8% (exact + fuzzy) with the full existing test suite (28 files, all green) plus new regression coverage in tests/test_sc_template_library.py for both the bridged cases and the equipment-swap cases that must keep failing. The remaining ~7.8k unmatched references are mostly genuine: sport-specific conditioning/skill work with no exercises.json equivalent by design (swim drills, sled sprints/pulls by distance, running intervals, hangboard/campus-board drills, shadowboxing/bag rounds), plus a real handful of common gym lifts exercises.json has no entry for at all yet (plain barbell shrug, triceps pushdown, seated calf raise machine, ab crunch machine, barbell skull crusher, dumbbell lateral raise, cable glute kickback) - adding those is a separate content task, not a matching fix, and wasn't guessed at here.
